parsed.label: capital letter after punctuation or line break
parsed.trigger_hypothesis: The neuron activates strongly positive when a capital letter token (like 'P', 'David', '-T') appears immediately after a punctuation mark (comma, period, newline) or a line break, indicating the start of a new sentence or proper noun. It activates strongly negative when a lowercase letter token (like 'h', 'P' as part of a word) appears after a space or within a word, indicating continuation of a word or lowercase start.
parsed.output_hypothesis: The neuron may signal the start of a new sentence or proper noun, potentially influencing the model to generate capitalized tokens or proper names.
alternatives: The neuron detects proper nouns or names specifically.
The neuron responds to the token 'P' in any context, with sign determined by surrounding punctuation.
parsed.adapter_changes: State changes are minimal; slight variations exist but no systematic pattern reversal, suggesting the trigger is robust across modifications.

proper noun after comma vs common word
newline start with capital vs lowercase
capital 'P' as start vs within word
comma then capital vs comma then lowercase
period then space capital vs no period
colon then capital vs colon then lowercase
